###### # Body ######
BEGIN_PGML Is [`2`] a solution to the inequality [`\frac{z+3}{z-1}\lt\sqrt{18z}\text{?}`]
>> [@DataTable( [ [ PGML('[`\dfrac{z+3}{z-1}`]'), PGML('[`{}\lt{}`]'), PGML('[`\sqrt{18z}`]'), ], [ PGML('[_]{5}{2}'), PGML('[`{}\wonder{\lt}{}`]'), PGML('[_]{6}{2}'), ], ], align => 'rcl', valign => 'middle',);@]* <<
[_]{$yesno}{5}
END_PGML
########## # Solution ##########
BEGIN_PGML_SOLUTION We have to substitute [`2`] in for [`z`] and simplify each side:
[``` \begin{aligned} \frac{z+3}{z-1}\amp\lt\sqrt{18z}\\ \frac{\substitute{2}+3}{\substitute{2}-1}\amp\wonder{\lt}\sqrt{18(\substitute{2})}\\ \frac{\highlight{5}}{\highlight{1}}\amp\wonder{\lt}\sqrt{\highlight{36}}\\ \highlight{5}\amp\confirm{\lt}\highlight{6} \end{aligned} ```]
Since [`5\lt6`] is true, [`2`] is indeed a solution to this inequality.
END_PGML_SOLUTION
